title: One voice reads, another teaches
statement: Read the text in one voice and the teaching around it in another, keeping each role's voice the same in every lesson so students hear them as different things.
detail: A reading course's voice table gives each grade deliberate voices for the voice that teaches and the voice that reads the book, with the reason written in the code: keeping the two voices distinct is how a student hears the story and the teaching as separate things. One grade's reading voice was chosen so that a made-up teaching case and real evidence sound different. A voice law fails the same role cut in different voices across lessons, the shape of an incident in which one word's card came out in a completely different voice, while a single page may still mix voices across roles.
against: one grade keeps a single voice for every role, only because its audio had already shipped and re-keying would invalidate measured clips; and one grade's shipped voices differ from its row in the voice table, kept for consistency within the unit as an open ruling (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0195-g5-book-lane-secret-garden-closed.qmd`, lines 73-77). One grade keeps a single voice for every role, only because its audio had already shipped (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0182-audio-voice-rulings.qmd`), and the same voice across pages is checked only in part, by a validator that rejects unknown role names (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0194-g3-book-audio-clip-conventions.qmd`).
